class.name: FoliagePainter3D
class.brief_description: Paints one or more kinds of vegetation onto other meshes with a brush, in the editor.
class.description: [FoliagePainter3D] holds a list of [member layers] (vegetation types, each a [FoliageLayer]). It is the counterpart to [FoliageSpawner3D]'s procedural box-volume scattering: instead of filling a volume automatically, instances are painted, erased, or placed/removed one at a time directly onto the actual surface geometry of any [MeshInstance3D] or [Landscape3D] in the scene, using the brush tool that appears in the 3D viewport's toolbar while a [FoliagePainter3D] is selected. Add at least one [FoliageLayer] to [member layers] before using the brush, and give it a mesh via [member FoliageLayer.lod_levels] (a fresh layer already has three default LOD levels; just assign a [Mesh] to at least the first one). The brush toolbar lets you choose which layers it paints with at once, its radius and density, and one of four modes: - [b]Paint[/b]: click or drag over a mesh surface to scatter instances of the active layers within the brush, with random scale, rotation, and normal deviation controlled per layer (see [member FoliageLayer.min_scale], [member FoliageLayer.random_rotation], [member FoliageLayer.align_to_normal_amount], and [member FoliageLayer.random_tilt_degrees]). - [b]Erase[/b]: click or drag to remove instances of the active layers found within the brush. - [b]Place Single[/b]: click to insert exactly one instance at the exact clicked point. - [b]Remove Single[/b]: click to delete the single closest instance to the clicked point. Painting looks at [MeshInstance3D] geometry directly (no physics bodies or collision shapes are required on a painted-on mesh); a [Landscape3D] target is raycast through its own physics collision shape instead, since it keeps one in sync automatically anyway. [b]LOD levels:[/b] each [FoliageLayer] renders through a chain of [FoliageLODLevel]s (see [member FoliageLayer.lod_levels]), e.g. a detailed mesh up close and a cheaper one (or none at all) far away, each with its own visibility/fade distance range and optional material override - all levels of a layer share the exact same painted instance transforms, only their mesh/material/range differ. This lets nearby dense foliage (e.g. grass) switch to a simpler representation, or disappear, at a much shorter distance than larger background vegetation. [b]Cell chunking:[/b] each layer's instances are stored split into a grid of cells on the local XZ plane, sized by [member cell_size]; each non-empty (layer, cell) pair is rendered through one internal [MultiMeshInstance3D] per LOD level. A single giant [MultiMesh] would always be drawn in full once any part of it is visible, since the renderer only culls whole nodes by their bounding box; splitting it into many small, tightly-bounded cells lets the renderer's normal per-node frustum culling skip whole cells that are off-screen instead. Set [member cell_size] before painting a large area — changing it later does not move already-painted instances into the new grid. Enable [member debug_show_cells] to visualize the resulting cell boundaries in the 3D viewport. [b]GPU culling:[/b] [member gpu_culling] replaces that scheme with per-instance culling on the GPU. Cells stay exactly as they are - they are still what the brush edits and what gets saved - but they stop being drawn: each layer's instances are gathered into one flat buffer, and each frame a compute pass tests each of them against the camera frustum and against its LOD level's distance band, compacting the survivors into one indirect [MultiMesh] per level (see [member MultiMesh.use_indirect]). Cell chunking can only skip whole cells, so a cell that is half on screen still draws every instance in it; the compute pass drops individual instances instead, and picks each one's LOD level by its own distance rather than the distance to the cell it happens to sit in. See [member gpu_culling] for its requirements and limitations. While instances are usually added and removed through the brush, [method insert_instance], [method remove_instance], and [method add_instance] are also available for scripted or procedural editing.

method.name: add_instance
method.description: Appends a new instance with the given local-space [param transform] to the layer at [param layer_index], in the cell at [param cell] (see [member cell_size]), and returns its index within that cell. Equivalent to calling [method insert_instance] with an index equal to that cell's current instance count.

method.name: get_layer
method.description: Returns the [FoliageLayer] at [param layer_index] in [member layers].

method.name: get_layer_count
method.description: Returns the number of layers in [member layers].

method.name: insert_instance
method.description: Inserts a new instance with the given local-space [param transform] at [param index] within the cell at [param cell] (see [member cell_size]) in the layer at [param layer_index], shifting any existing instances of that cell at or after [param index] up by one. [param index] is clamped to the cell's current instance count, so passing that count appends the instance. The cell is created automatically if it doesn't exist yet.

method.name: remove_instance
method.description: Removes instance [param index] from the cell at [param cell] in the layer at [param layer_index], shifting any subsequent instances of that cell down by one. The cell itself is freed automatically once it has no instances left.

members.member: The size (in meters, on the local XZ plane) of the grid cells that each layer's instances are chunked into. See the class description for why this matters. Larger values mean fewer, bigger cells (coarser culling, less overhead); smaller values mean finer-grained culling at the cost of more internal [MultiMeshInstance3D] nodes. It should generally stay well above the brush radius and above [member FoliageLayer.min_instance_spacing], which only checks for nearby instances within the same cell and its immediate neighbors.

If [code]true[/code], the editor gizmo draws the bounds of every non-empty cell (see [member cell_size]). See [b]Cell chunking[/b] in the class description. Off by default since it can clutter the viewport once a large area has been painted.

If [code]true[/code], visibility is decided per instance by a compute pass on the GPU instead of per cell by the renderer. See [b]GPU culling[/b] in the class description. Nothing painted is lost when this is toggled: cells remain the stored form either way, so the brush, undo/redo and saving are unaffected. This pays off when a lot of instances share the screen with a lot of instances that are off it: dense grass over a wide area, or a small [member cell_size] that would otherwise cost many draw calls. It does not pay off for a handful of instances, where the compute dispatch costs more than it saves. It also costs memory, since each LOD level gets a buffer sized for the case where every instance of its layer is visible at once. [b]Note:[/b] Requires the Forward+ or Mobile rendering method; the Compatibility renderer cannot draw indirect [MultiMesh]es and this falls back to cell chunking there. [b]Note:[/b] This path has no LOD cross-fade. Overlapping [member FoliageLODLevel.visibility_range_begin]/[member FoliageLODLevel.visibility_range_end] bands are collapsed into contiguous ones so that every instance is drawn by exactly one level, and [member FoliageLODLevel.visibility_range_fade_mode] is ignored. [b]Note:[/b] Only the first four entries of each layer's [member FoliageLayer.lod_levels] are rendered, culling follows one camera: the viewport's current [Camera3D] at runtime, or the first 3D editor viewport in the editor (so other split views are culled against that one), and instances get no motion vectors (so they are not anti-aliased by TAA).

The vegetation types this node can paint. Each entry is a [FoliageLayer] with its own [member FoliageLayer.lod_levels], randomization settings, and brush density/spacing. Add and configure entries from the Inspector, then select this node to paint with the brush tool in the 3D viewport.
